text: `parseDigits` returns `NaN`. When `parseInt(str, 10)` is already `NaN`, it falls back to accumulating digit characters into the string `value`; if nothing matches (no Latin digits, no hanidec chars, no other numbering-system code points), `value` stays `""` and the final `parseInt("", 10)` yields `NaN`.
It returns `[matches, {}]` where `matches` is `null` (the result of `input.match(regex)` when there is no match) — i.e. `[null, {}]`. The caller then checks `if (!matches) return [null, parsed]`.
It returns `LocalZone.instance` (the fallback `defaultZone || LocalZone.instance`), not null.
It logs the error to the console (`console.error(e)`) and returns the string `"[error]"`.

It builds an HTML page: `"

Some Luxon examples

"` plus an intro paragraph plus `"" + examples.join("") + "
"`, and assigns that to `document.body.innerHTML`.
It resets the internal `defaultZone` to `null` (`if (!z) { defaultZone = null; }`), so `Settings.defaultZone` then falls back to `LocalZone.instance`.
It is abstract: `get type()` throws `new ZoneIsAbstractError()` (subclasses override it to return their type string).

It builds `zone = new FixedOffsetZone(matches.Z)` (the parsed numeric offset in minutes). If `Z` is undefined it falls back to `IANAZone.create(matches.z)` when `matches.z` is defined, otherwise `null`.

Fixed: Interval.fromISO now catches the throwOnInvalid exceptions from the DateTime/Duration parses and falls back to the duration-based interpretation, so with Settings.throwOnInvalid = true it still returns valid intervals (e.g. "2016-05-25/P1D") and only throws for genuinely unparsable input. Also corrected the invalid explanation string to "can't be parsed as ISO 8601". Interval suite: 128/128 passing.

Fixed: objToLocalTS now does `d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)` instead of shifting the overflowed year, so crossing the 100 barrier through February (e.g. 0099-12-31 + 61 days => 0100-03-02) is correct.

Fixed: isInDST now compares against `this.set({ month: 1, day: 1 })` (January 1st, standard time) instead of keeping the day-of-month, which landed inside 1974's Jan 6–Oct 27 DST window. 1974-01-06 through 1974-10-27 now report true and the rest of the year false.

Fixed: the casual and accurate conversion matrices were missing `years.quarters` (and `quarters.seconds`), so normalizing/shifting year<->quarter or quarter<->second pairs produced NaN. All unit pairs now convert; duration suite 114/114 passing.
Fixed: padStart now pads the absolute value and re-attaches the minus sign, so negative years render as "-0005" instead of "00-5" (DateTime#toISODate/toISO/toFormat).
Fixed: FixedOffsetZone.isValid now returns `isNumber(this.fixed)`, so a zone built with a non-numeric offset is invalid and DateTimes in it are invalid too.
Hour 24 is valid only when the rest of the time is exactly zero: `hour === 24 && minute === 0 && second === 0 && millisecond === 0` (otherwise hours must be 0–23).

The `format` argument accepts the offset-format names used by `formatOffset`: "short" (e.g. "+05:30"), "narrow" (e.g. "+5:30"), and "techie" (e.g. "+0530"); anything else falls back to the short form.
